transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess I'm here because things have been pretty difficult lately. Ever since they made me the acting workflow lead at the warehouse, I've just been... well, I walk in the doors already tense. 

I'm catching myself snapping at people over stupid little SAP errors. And I'm actually missing cycle-count deadlines, which I never used to do. It's just taking a lot out of me. By the time I get home, I'm too drained to even go play basketball or, you know, work on my sketches like I usually do. I just don't have the energy for any of it anymore.
When exactly did you start noticing this tension and low energy - did it begin right around the time you took on the acting workflow lead role, or had you been feeling this way before that?

It definitely wasn't before that. The lead role actually started right after we had a team merger at the warehouse. I'd say within the first month or two of that transition, I could just tell I wasn't handling work the way I normally do.

Do you notice this same tension or worry showing up in other parts of your life outside of work - like with family, finances, or other day-to-day things - or does it seem to be triggered specifically by the work situation?

No, it really seems to just be about work. I mean, my family life is fine, and I'm not stressing over money or anything like that. It's just... when I think about the warehouse, or when I'm there, that's when I feel it. Outside of that, I'm just tired from dealing with it all day.

Even on days off when you're away from the warehouse entirely, do you still feel down or find that you've lost interest in things you normally enjoy, or does your mood lift once you're away from work?

I'm not really sure. I mean, the actual stress of being there goes away when I'm off, but... I wouldn't say my mood completely bounces back either. Like I said, I'm just so drained. Even on a Saturday, I still don't really have the drive to go shoot hoops or get my sketchpad out. I mostly just kind of sit around, trying to recover from the week.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately - trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up much earlier than usual?
No, my sleep hasn't really changed. I mean, I'm tired, so I fall asleep okay, and I don't think I'm waking up in the middle of the night or anything. I just sleep my normal hours.
Have you been feeling unusually down on yourself, guilty, or hopeless about things in general, even when you're not thinking about work?

No, not really. I don't feel guilty or... down on myself, no. And I wouldn't say I feel hopeless about life in general. It's really just the job that's getting to me. I'm frustrated with how things are going at the warehouse, but I don't feel like everything else is pointless or anything like that.

When you're at work or even anticipating going in, do you notice physical signs of anxiety - like a racing heart, muscle tension, restlessness, or a sense of dread - along with the irritability you've described?

No, I haven't really noticed any of that. My heart doesn't race, and I'm not really restless. It's just... I get really annoyed and frustrated when I'm there. But I don't get that physical panic feeling or dread, no.

When you're dealing with the workflow lead situation, would you describe your main emotional reaction as more worry and anxiety about how things will turn out, or more irritability and frustration without much worry attached to it?

It's definitely more on the irritability side. I'm not really worried about it... like, I don't sit there feeling anxious about how things are going to turn out. It's just straight frustration when I have to deal with him and the way things are running right now.

Aside from feeling drained, do you find that you generally don't enjoy things the way you used to - like basketball or sketching - even when you have the energy and time to do them, or is it mainly that you're too tired to start?

No, I still enjoy them. When I actually get around to shooting hoops or picking up my sketchbook, I like it just fine. It's really just the energy part. I'm just so drained from dealing with work that by the time I get home, I just want to crash. But the enjoyment is still there if I can get myself to do it.
You mentioned this started within a month or two of the team merger and new lead role - overall, how many months has it now been that you've been feeling this way?
It's been about four months. Yeah, right around four months since they merged the inventory teams and put me in that acting workflow lead role. That's when all this really started.
